summary: Whalen Lai works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University (~1968-1975), holding posts at UC Davis (~1977) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1993).

Whitney Cox is an Indologist who studied at the University of Virginia (~1993-1997) and at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~2000-2006). He held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2003).

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. He completed a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Upper Canada College, the University of Toronto (~1934-1938), and Princeton University (~1946-1948). He served as director (所長) at Harvard University (~1964-1973).

Philosopher Wilfrid Sellars studied at Lycée Montaigne, Göttingen, Michigan, Buffalo, and Oriel College. He held posts at Iowa (1938-1946), Minnesota (1947-1958), Yale (1958-1963), Pittsburgh (1963-1989), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Wilhelm Deecke was a linguist who studied at Katharineum, Leipzig, and Berlin, learning under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held teaching posts at Katharineum (1852-1855) and Ernestinenschule (1855-1870).

Wilhelm Geiger was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. After earning his PhD under Friedrich von Spiegel at Erlangen-Nuremberg, he held professorships at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1891) and Munich (1920-1924).

Wilhelm Grube was a Sinologist and linguist who studied under Vasily Vasiliev and Georg von der Gabelentz, attending Leipzig University (~1878-1880). He later served as an associate professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1892-1908).

Wilhelm Halbfass worked in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the University of Göttingen (~1967-1970), the University of Hamburg (1981-1982), the University of Pennsylvania (~1973-2000), and the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (attested 1991).

Wilhelm Pertsch was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber (1850), at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851-1854), and under Rudolf von Roth (~1853-1855).
Wilhelm Rau was an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts at Leipzig University, Goethe University Frankfurt (~1953-1957), and the University of Marburg (~1957-1988).
Wilhelm Scherer was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1858-1860). He held posts at the University of Vienna (~1868-1872) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1877-1886).

Wilhelm Schulze was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1892-1895), the University of Göttingen (~1895-1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902-1932).

Wilhelm Streitberg was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Leipzig University (~1884-1888). He later held posts at the University of Münster (~1901-1909), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1909-1920), and Leipzig University (~1920-1925).
Wilhelm Wackernagel was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824-1827). He held a long-term academic post at the University of Basel (~1833-1869).

Wilhelm von Humboldt was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Frankfurt an der Oder, Göttingen, and Jena. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin in 1810 and also held a post there.
Will B. Miller is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso, and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University (~1990-1993) and the University of Cambridge (~1993-1997), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2003).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tamalpais High School, Stanford University, Princeton University, and Harvard University. He held a post at the University of Toronto (~1971-1999).
Willard J. Peterson is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology who was mentored by Denis Twitchett. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1981).
